title: Hybrid stream load simulator for protocol-diverse SSE/WebSocket workloads
creator: Aisha Nayar
description: Build a scalable, protocol-aware load simulator that models real client behavior across SSE and WebSocket endpoints and validates p95 token latency and tokens/sec at production scale. Unlike earlier mono-protocol drivers, this simulator will run hybrid scenarios (mixed SSE + WS + optional long-poll fallback), support session multiplexing, simulate KV-cache warm/cold patterns, inject controlled churn, and produce regression-safe histograms for automated p95 gating.
acceptance_criteria: Driver can sustain 12k concurrent streaming sessions (mix configurable: default 70% SSE / 30% WS) for 30m with <1% protocol-level error rate
End-to-end measured p95 token latency (client receive to server token generation) exported to Prometheus and visible on Grafana
Tokens/sec baseline measurement flow that reproduces within +/-8% over three repeated runs in identical infra
Automated regression detector flags a test run when p95 increases by >=10% relative to stored baseline and opens an issue with attached histograms
KV-cache-aware flows show measurable difference in model-side token generation time (hot vs cold) and driver can tag sessions accordingly
Runs include chaos knobs: random disconnects, pause/resume of streams, bandwidth throttling and these are configurable per-scenario
design_notes: Principles: reproducibility, observable histograms, and low client-side variance. Use deterministic user behavior seeds and a small library of ‘conversation templates’ with variable token-length distributions (short bursts, long form continuations, question-answer pairs). Token pacing must follow a configurable waveform generator (Poisson burst + steady-state) to approximate real production mixes. Each synthetic session will track per-session metadata: sequence id, cache state (hot/warm/cold), tenant id, and affinity bucket. The agent will support TLS, keep-alive, and should reuse connections where realistic. We will record both client-side receive timestamps and server-provided token generation timestamps when available for precise E2E measurements.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: PoC single-protocol WebSocket driver (Go) with token pacing and deterministic seeds
Phase 2: Add SSE path and a protocol-agnostic session abstraction, implement multiplexing and long-poll fallback
Phase 3: KV-cache-aware session tagging and synthetic cache-warmup orchestration
Phase 4: Autoscale runner on Kubernetes (Jobs + HPA for controller) and integrate k8s-job-scheduler for large fanout
Phase 5: Integrate Prometheus metrics export, t-digest based histogram sinks, and Grafana dashboard panels
Phase 6: Implement regression detector service that compares current run histograms to stored baseline and auto-creates ENG tickets + alerts PagerDuty when regression is high impact
telemetry_and_alerting: Export metrics: tokens_per_sec, e2e_token_latency_seconds{quantile}, server_token_gen_ms_summary, connection_setup_ms, socket_error_rate, fd_usage, kv_cache_hit_ratio, session_churn_rate. Use Prometheus remote_write to our perf-cluster. Store histograms using t-digest summarizer and persist baseline digests in s3://redwood-perf/baselines/hybrid-stream. Regression rules: detect relative p95 increase >=10% OR absolute p95 increase >=50ms with >=5% of runs failing. When triggered, create GitHub issue template with attached run metadata and link to Grafana snapshot; also send PagerDuty alert to SRE on-call. All dashboards must include run-id and seed to allow reruns.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created — initial scope and acceptance criteria agreed in sync with PM (Jorge Alvarez) and Design (Priya Rao).

2026-02-24: Prototype WebSocket driver implemented (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/perf/hybrid-sim). Basic token pacing and deterministic seed working locally. PR#182 created for initial review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/182

2026-03-01: Added SSE support and protocol abstraction. Early load tests show connection churn handling is the main resource pressure point on client pods. Logged infra follow-up ENG-481021 for socket fd tuning.
2026-03-05: Integrated t-digest histogram exporter and verified p95 calculations with sample runs. Created Grafana dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/stream/hybrid-load (draft).

2026-03-08: Ran 2k-session mixed protocol run on perf-cluster; observed median tokens/sec per-node matches expectations but p95 spikes correlate with periodic cache evictions. Added KV-cache warmup orchestration to mitigate. Recording logs to s3://redwood-perf/runs/2026-03-08-hybrid/

2026-03-10: Regression detector MVP integrated; currently compares run digests to baseline and posts results to #perf-alerts Slack channel. Need to tune thresholds and persist baselines. Assigned follow-ups for baseline operator and run orchestration improvements.
